text:
Marathon Petroleum stock dropped 0.58% today to $371.67, extending a sharp decline over the past week that has wiped out nearly $41 per share since mid-November. The selloff appears tied to escalating geopolitical risk in the Middle East—Iran has launched attacks on U.S. military installations in Kuwait and the Persian Gulf, and the IEA warned that confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable energy corridor has been "crushed" by the conflict. For a refiner, this kind of regional instability typically creates uncertainty about oil supply and pricing, even though crude prices remain in the $89–$93 range and refineries are running near full capacity (95.7%).

The timing of the decline also matters: the stock began falling sharply on November 18, the same day the geopolitical warnings escalated, suggesting investors are pricing in concern about potential disruption to Middle Eastern oil flows that could roil refining margins and crude availability in coming weeks.
